finding.title: Fix make audit check 15/15's self-comparing awk so cross-feature deep imports are ever detected
finding.rule: Rule 0 (checker must detect what it claims); Rule 2; AG-11
finding.why: match($1,...) extracts the feature name from the FILE PATH ($1, e.g. 'dashboard'). match($0,...) is meant to extract the feature name of the IMPORTED module, but $0 is 'path:line:content' and $1 is a literal prefix of $0, so match($0,...) finds that same 'dashboard' substring inside the path prefix before it ever reaches the import statement — a[1] and b[1] are therefore always identical and 'if (a[1] != b[1])' can never be true for any input. I confirmed this by piping track_stat_grid.dart's real cross-feature import (dashboard deep-importing scheduler's daily_task.dart, not via a barrel) through the literal pipeline (0 lines out) and by isolating the awk step directly (a[1]=dashboard, b[1]=dashboard). A rough repo-wide count of the same import shape this check should be flagging runs into the hundreds (e.g. tracks→scheduler ×31, dashboard→scheduler ×26, settings→account ×23 lines by a similar grep). `make audit PASSED` reads as 'Rule 2 is at least being warned about'; in reality check 15 has never printed a single violation since it was written, so the 'warn-only, pending Wave-2 fix' backlog it exists to size has been completely invisible the whole time — new cross-feature deep imports can be added freely with zero signal.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to extract the imported feature from the import string specifically (e.g. operate on a field after stripping the 'path:line:' prefix, or grep the 'package:learning_tracker/features/X/' substring in the import text only) rather than re-scanning the whole line. Add a fixture test: one known cross-feature-deep-import line must warn, one same-feature multi-segment import must not.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15/15 prints a WARN line citing lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/track_stat_grid.dart:8 (or the fix documents an explicit, reviewed barrel exemption for domain models) on the current tree
a shell/unit test pins the checker against a same-feature multi-segment import fixture and asserts it produces no false positive
